key_insight: Small exchange-pulse area errors can undermine encoded quantum algorithms, with systematic errors accumulating quadratically in circuit depth and jitter accumulating linearly.
engineering_relevance: Exchange-only spin-qubit control needs roughly 8–10 significant bits for common-mode pulse-area accuracy, alongside leakage mitigation and sufficient exchange speed to limit magnetic-gradient effects.
method: Compiled VQE, QAOA, Grover search, phase estimation and a distance-3 repetition code into exchange pulses on up to six encoded qubits.
Perturbed pulse areas using systematic fractional errors, offsets and per-pulse jitter.
Evaluated algorithm accuracy, leakage, compilation sensitivity and control-resolution requirements.
evidence_signal: In the tested circuits, chemical accuracy failed near a systematic fractional error of 0.006 for H₂ and LiH, while 498–1,216-pulse circuits lost 5% of success probability at errors of 0.003–0.009.
watch_item: Thresholds varied by factors of 2–8 across compilations, and leakage-blind error correction could worsen performance; these small-circuit results are not universal fault-tolerance thresholds.
paper_title: Pulse-timing errors in exchange-only spin qubits: how one control imperfection propagates to VQE, QAOA and fault-tolerance primitives
